thread:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: tenant=orca (dedicated-vpc) high tail latency and growing request backlog on pool:dedicated-us-west-2-3. p99 latency > 6s for last 5m.
ryan_oncall: seeing it, paging in. grabbing context now. 
kim_sre: I can see queue_depth spiking on scheduler shard 7, backlog dominated by long-sequence requests (~> 4000 tokens). Looks like a single large request pattern is starving smaller requests.
zoe_runtime: confirmation: KV cache hits fine, but batch formation is waiting for either max_batch_tokens or timeout. Current tenant max_batch_tokens=8192 (default override). That's letting big requests block.
ryan_oncall: ok quick mitigation idea: set ORCA tenant scheduler to enforce smaller max_batch_tokens and enable short-first priority so short requests get preference. Can we push a soft config change?
marta_acct: pinging Orca account team — Marta here. FYI customer is seeing timeouts in their internal UI; SLA-sensitive. They just raised support ticket.
aaron_cs: Orca reports degraded UX for search and chat flows. They're asking ETA on fix.
zoe_runtime: I can do a canary change on one scheduler shard. Plan: set tenant.override.max_batch_tokens=1024 on shard 7, scheduler.policy="short-first", queue_capacity=300. Roll for 1 shard then observe 5m.
ryan_oncall: 👍 do it. Post the exact command you run.
zoe_runtime: running now.
```
# canary patch
curl -s -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/tenants/orca/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"scheduler":{"max_batch_tokens":1024,"priority":"short-first","queue_capacity":300},"_meta":{"reason":"tail latency mitigation - canary"}}'
```
zoe_runtime: returned 202. Patch applied to shard=7.
inc-bot: CONFIG_CHANGE: tenant=orca config applied on shard=7 by zoe_runtime at 3898765600.
kim_sre: watching metrics. p95 down from 2.1s -> 800ms on shard7 within 60s. p99 trending down but still noisy. Good sign.
luis_infra: autoscaler triggered a 1-instance burst on dedicated-us-west-2-3 to help throughput (policy: emergency-burst).
ryan_oncall: rolling change to remaining shards but staggered to avoid flapping. next shard in 60s.
zoe_runtime: note — we also toggle tenant-level "prefer_small_requests" flag to true to bias scheduler. Command: `PATCH /tenants/orca/scheduler?prefer_small=true`
ryan_oncall: applied on shards 8 and 9.
aaron_cs: Orca on call just acknowledged, saying immediate improvement in chat latency. They're holding until you confirm stable.
kim_sre: let's keep monitoring for 15m. Also check for any regressions in throughput or token cost. Reducing max_batch_tokens can increase per-token cost.
marta_acct: Orca asks: will this change be persistent? They want a postmortem and to know if config will be reverted.
zoe_runtime: this is temporary mitigation. After 30m stable we will evaluate: either keep new scheduler knobs as an agreed tenant profile or revert and explore longer-term model/quantization changes.
ryan_oncall: heads-up: I see one weird long-tail request still at p99 ~4s from shard 12 (different shard). Might be a different tenant call path calling a huge system prompt — investigating.
kim_sre: For visibility, capturing relevant logs: 
```
/var/log/runtime/shard-7/orca.log | grep -E "BATCH_FORMED|DELAYED_REQUEST|MAX_BATCH_TOKENS"
```
kim_sre: logs show large batches being split post-change, and queue wait times for small requests dropped ~85%.
luis_infra: infra note: burst instances will be charged against dedicated commit; created emergency-burst to avoid 503s. Inform finance if sustained.
aaron_cs: Orca confirms 10-15% drop in error rate and p99 improved for interactive endpoints. They asked for ETA on full cluster mitigation.
ryan_oncall: continuing roll across the 6 shards for this pool with 45s spacing. We'll stop if CPU > 85% or error rate increases.
zoe_runtime: currently rolled 4/6 shards. No CPU blowups. p99 cluster-wide down from 6s -> ~1.1s.
kim_sre: starting a short meeting with product/CS to coordinate customer comms and TTR. I'll jot action items.
marta_acct: thanks — I'll coordinate an interim note to Orca: "We applied scheduler-level mitigations (max_batch_tokens reduced, short-first scheduling) to improve latency. Monitoring closely; temporary measure"
aaron_cs: customer asked about root cause — looks like traffic pattern change with more long-sequence requests from a data pipeline. Can we confirm?
zoe_runtime: preliminary logs indicate a spike of bulk-export calls (system user: export-batcher) at 15:12 UTC that generated many 3000-8000 token requests over ~6m. Those coincided with the onset.
ryan_oncall: action items: (1) keep mitigation until postmortem, (2) follow up with Orca about throttling export-batcher or moving it to dedicated job host, (3) evaluate tenant profile for persistent max_batch_tokens cap.
kim_sre: will file incident ticket and link config changes, metrics, and raw logs. Assigning severity=2.
zoe_runtime: I'll prepare a follow-up plan: try adaptive batching thresholds that detect long-request floods and isolate them into separate queue. That avoids manual caps.
luis_infra: if we need, we can spin a temporary isolated pool for Orca exports to avoid impacting interactive paths. Requires infra lead and billing signoff.
ryan_oncall: agreed. For now, mitigation in place. Monitoring window extended to 60m.
inc-bot: RESOLVED? not yet — monitoring. Last update at 3898765987.
ryan_oncall: closing loop — will post final incident summary in incidents channel once we have postmortem and timeline. Thanks all :thumbsup:
